legend: ✅ built in, or in an official package of the same project (named) · ⚠️ partial, opt-in, Premium (paid), with a caveat, or through a third-party package (named) · ❌ not built in · 🔜 planned by the maintainers, no code yet · — does not apply. The RxDB column is rxdb 17.6.0 (npm `latest`, October 2026), decided from its source code at that tag, from runs of the published package and from every page of rxdb.info; Premium plugins are closed source, so their cells follow the docs. The syncom column is this repository.

serverLicense.text: MIT: hosting (`sync.unit()`) is in the same package

premiumSplit.text: no split: every feature is in the MIT package

premiumTerms.text: MIT: no term, token or usage limit

collectionLimit.source: src/schema.js (no cap); scratch check: open() with 40 entities over createMemoryFsi()

phoneHome.text: none: no network code beyond the injected transport
phoneHome.source: src/ (no fetch, iframe or beacon); src/wrpc.js

deps.source: package.json (no `dependencies`); scripts/size.js:109-121 (fails on any bare import in a browser bundle)

impl.text: JavaScript, CommonJS, no build step; `src/` ships as is
impl.detail: Checked with Node 24.14.1: the root entry exposes only `default` to ESM, while /wrpc, /idb, /search and /contracts expose their names. The docs' `import { open }` examples are all in bundler contexts (docs/guide/browser.md, wrpc.md#in-the-browser).

types.text: hand-written `.d.ts`, tsd-tested; collection names typed, record data `unknown`

size.text: 65.0 KB min+gzip: the browser entry, the whole engine
size.detail: Measured by `pnpm size` on 2026-10-24 (features/enhance-crdt-engine). CommonJS is not tree-shaken, so storage, schema, queries, the op log, signing, the sync protocol and the list, text and tree engines all come with `open()`. No validator library is included in either column (injected / wrapped separately).

sizeSync.text: 65.6 KB min+gzip with the wrpc link adapter

sizeGate.text: `pnpm size` fails CI when the browser entry passes 65 KB

node.text: ≥22; persists with `node:fs`; CI on Node 22 and 24

browserReq.text: secure context, OPFS, Web Crypto with Ed25519 and RSA-OAEP
browserReq.detail: docs/guide/browser.md names OPFS and Web Crypto but not Ed25519 specifically; which browser versions expose Ed25519 in Web Crypto was not checked here. OPFS writes use `createWritable()`.

worker.text: a storage served from a worker to its tabs is the planned follow-up
worker.detail: The browser half has no `window` dependency (src/lock.js:87 treats `self` as a browser), but running inside a worker is not tested. wrpc's `WrpcClientProxy` can already share one connection from a SharedWorker.

reactNative.text: not a target: no React Native backend or Web Crypto shim

capacitor.text: not tested; a Capacitor `fsi` adapter is yours to write

electron.text: not documented or tested; no IPC bridge
electron.detail: The main process is Node.js and a renderer is a browser, so either half may run there; nothing checks it.

multiTab.text: one tab per storage: `open()` holds a Web Lock, a second tab gets `LOCKED`
multiTab.note: There are no cross-tab change events and no read-only open: the other tabs wait for the lock (`lock: 'wait'`) or route reads and writes to the owner through a `BroadcastChannel`.
multiTab.detail: Two storages over one directory would mint the same sequence numbers, which is why the lock exists (src/lock.js:4-9).

leader.text: no election API; `lock: 'wait'` hands the storage to the next tab

storageContract.detail: Optional `sync` (fsync, used by `durable: true`) and `create` (exclusive create, used by the lock). Everything above bytes — records, log, chain, catalog, indexes, queries — is the engine's and identical on every backend.

customBackend.text: five functions; `tests/suites/fsi.js` is the contract as a test
customBackend.source: docs/guide/backends.md#your-own; tests/suites/fsi.js; src/backend.js:35-82 (the memory adapter, ~45 lines)
customBackend.detail: The contract suite lives in the repository, not in the npm package (`files` excludes tests/). An adapter must make `write` whole-file and visible to the next `read`, and `list` return file names, sorted.

memoryBackend.text: `createMemoryFsi()`: a `Map` of files; Node and browser
memoryBackend.detail: Files are kept as JSON strings, so reads still parse; two storages over one memory fsi with different paths form a mesh in one process (how the sync-engine suite runs).

indexeddb.text: `@alexify/syncom/idb` `createIdbFsi()`: each file a row keyed `[dir, name]`
indexeddb.detail: One IndexedDB transaction per file write, resolved on `complete`; `durable: true` is a no-op there.

opfs.text: the default browser backend; async `createWritable()`, main thread or worker
opfs.detail: One file per record, per chain block and per log batch, written through the async API, not sync access handles. RxDB's own storage article notes that one file per document is the slow way to write to OPFS (https://rxdb.info/articles/localstorage-indexeddb-cookies-opfs-sqlite-wasm.html).

localStorage.text: none shipped; an `fsi` over it would be five functions

nodeFs.text: the default under Node: `node:fs/promises`, plain JSON files

expoFs.text: none; not a target, an `fsi` is injectable

storageTrialLimits.text: none: every backend is in the MIT package

storageWrappers.text: an `fsi` can wrap an `fsi` (bytes only); document transforms are hooks

remoteStorage.text: none; a peer replicates a copy instead

memoryMapped.text: none; `cache.max` entries and the catalog stay in memory

openCost.text: the catalog (every id, indexed values) and the retained log, into memory
openCost.detail: A missing or unresumable catalog is rebuilt by reading every file in data/. The log keeps 10,000 ops by default.

durability.text: log batch first, then the record; `durable: true` fsyncs each file (node:fs)
durability.note: Files are rewritten in place, with no temp file and rename: on node:fs a crash mid-write can tear a record file, which then fails to parse until `repair(id)`.
durability.detail: `durable` fsyncs the file, not its directory. OPFS writables apply on close(); IndexedDB writes resolve on transaction complete. Without `durable`, the order in which the log file and the record file reach the disk is the OS's.

crashRecovery.text: replays the log's unsealed tail; a torn newest batch is dropped
crashRecovery.detail: Checked with scratch scripts on the memory fsi: a record file missing after its log append is rebuilt on reopen; a torn newest log batch is dropped with a `log.open.unreadable` warning. A batch whose record write failed stays unsealed and is replayed at every open until it lands.

exclusiveOpen.note: Two browser tabs are two instances: the second sees `LOCKED`, so one tab or a worker must own the storage.
exclusiveOpen.detail: A lockfile is stale when its pid is gone, or after 30 minutes when that cannot be told; per machine only.

integrityRepair.text: cold reads re-verified against the chain, torn files too (`INTEGRITY`); `repair(id)` replays the log
integrityRepair.note: `repair(id)` rebuilds a record while the log keeps a whole-record op for it; otherwise it is `UNRECOVERABLE`, and a peer's snapshot is the way back.
integrityRepair.detail: `integrity: 'lazy'` or `chain: false` turn the per-read check off. `repair` needs a whole-record op still in the log, otherwise `UNRECOVERABLE`.

quotas.text: none; past the log append a failed record file is held in memory and reported (`UNPERSISTED`)
quotas.detail: No `navigator.storage.persist()` request; the docs note the browser may evict OPFS.

onDiskFormat.text: plain JSON files: `data/<id>.json`, log batches, chain blocks, keys

writeFootprint.text: three per local write: log batch, chain block, record (two with `chain: false`)
writeFootprint.note: The chain is never compacted: one block file per local write and per applied batch, kept for good.
writeFootprint.detail: Measured: a record holding 45 bytes of data is a 509-byte file, its per-field clocks each carrying the 43-character node id.

docCache.text: `cache: { max: 5000 }` entries; a live `Record` pins its own (WeakRef)

attachments.text: none: JSON records only, no binary type

localDocs.text: only encrypted records stay local; no plain local documents

tombstoneCleanup.text: none: a tombstone keeps its file (data emptied) and catalog row
tombstoneCleanup.detail: Checked: a deleted record's file is `{ data: {}, meta: { deleted } }`, a purged one adds `purged`. The op log is bounded by retention; tombstone files and chain blocks are not.

deleteDatabase.text: no API; remove the directory yourself
deleteDatabase.source: src/storage.js; src/backend.js (no directory removal in the contract)

storageMigration.text: no tool; the same JSON files on every backend
storageMigration.detail: Copying every file from one fsi to another opens fine (checked memory to memory), but `list` names files only, so a copier must know the directory layout.

backup.text: no API; the Node directory is plain JSON, copy it closed
backup.note: Restoring an older copy of a node's directory is caught at the next hello (`REWOUND`): the node moves past the seqs its host holds and bootstraps the lost state back; writes made between the restore and that hello are lost to the host.

jsonDump.text: `snapshot()` pages out records with meta, tombstones too; `mergeSnapshot()` joins them
jsonDump.detail: This is the bootstrap API: no file format or schema stamp; a join is a CRDT merge recorded as `merge` ops, not an overwrite; encrypted records are left out (checked).

model.text: JSON records addressed by id; collections optional (`$type`)
model.detail: `Collection.get(id)` is `storage.get(id)` with no `$type` filter: `storage.Post.get(authorId)` returned the Author record (checked by running).

schemaless.text: no schema needed; `{}` is a bare collection

collectionNames.text: any non-empty string the storage does not answer to (`get`, `close`… refused at `open()`)

fieldNames.detail: A field named like a `Record` member (`save`, `data`, `delete`) stays in the data but is not a property of the live Record (warned as `record.shadowed`).

primaryKey.text: the record id, outside the data; the validator sees it under `idField`
primaryKey.detail: An `id` passed inside the data is not the record id: with a validator it is dropped from what is written, without one it is stored as a plain field (checked by running). Choose the id with `set(id, data)`.

idGeneration.text: `getId`: UUID by default; sync or async generator of your own

idRules.text: `[A-Za-z0-9_@-][A-Za-z0-9._@-]{0,127}`, checked on every write and peer op

schemaFormat.text: none of its own: a Standard Schema, a function, or `validator.compile()`
schemaFormat.detail: metaschema is the first-class fit (indexes, unique keys and the id field read off it); zod, valibot, arktype through `~standard`; JSON Schema or TypeBox through an injected Ajv.

validators.text: whatever you inject: metaschema, zod, valibot, arktype, ajv, TypeBox; none bundled

validationDefault.text: on for every entity with a `schema`; `validate: false` opts out
validationDefault.detail: A record written without `$type` (outside any collection) has no validator: `storage.set(id, …)` bypasses a collection's schema (checked by running).

validatorOutput.text: its value is written: defaults, aliases, stripped keys, decoders

tsInference.text: records are `unknown`; only collection names are typed

defaults.text: from the validator (metaschema `default`, zod `.default()`), folded into the op

nested.text: stored and validated; merged as one top-level register
nested.note: Concurrent edits to two keys of one nested object keep only one side, and `update({ 'a.b': 1 })` writes a top-level field named `a.b` (both documented in the Storage and Sync guides).

schemaVersion.text: `schema.version` on every op (`v`) and record (`meta.v`); snapshot hash

migration.text: lens on read (migrations, then the validator); `migrate()` rewrites, idempotent
migration.detail: `migrate()` re-adds counters and sets after the whole-record write (checked by running: `{ migrated: 1, counters: 1 }`, then `{ migrated: 0 }`).

readOld.text: read through the lens; writes allowed

peerVersions.text: the op carries `v`; lens for older, `ahead: 'apply' | 'hold'` for newer

bulk.text: none; one op per call (a batch is `Promise.all` of `insert()`)

upsert.detail: A whole-record write resets the record's counters and sets (docs/guide/sync.md#whole-record-writes-and-deletes).

unsetField.text: only by a whole-record `set()`; `undefined` in a delta is dropped
unsetField.detail: Checked by running: `update(id, { a: undefined })` left `a` as it was; `null` stores `null`.

modifyFn.text: no `modify(fn)`; `get()` then `swap()` in a retry loop

byQuery.text: none; `select().fetch()`, then one write per row

cas.text: `swap(id, changes, prev)` compares field values inside the write queue
cas.detail: Local only: a peer's concurrent write is merged, not refused.

localConflicts.text: one mutation queue; no local conflict errors

transactions.text: none; every write is one op on one record

counters.note: A counter that one node resets while another increments it does not converge to the intuitive value; see Guarantees and limits in the Sync guide.

lists.text: list fields: `splice()`, `setAt()`, `move()` (Fugue; a concurrent move lands once)

text.text: text fields: `splice()`/`updateText()` merge by position (Fugue); marks, cursors

crdtModel.text: built into every write: register, counter or OR-set per field

mergeGranularity.text: both kept: last writer wins per top-level field
mergeGranularity.detail: Checked by running on two storages exchanging ops. Overlaps the replication area's conflict row.

registerWinner.text: the later stamp `(ts, origin)`; a node's clock never falls behind what it saw

mergeHistory.text: op log beside the records, with retention; records keep per-field stamps

mergeBypass.text: none: every write is an op; mixing field kinds throws `FIELD_KIND`

conditionalOps.text: none that replicate; `swap()` is a local check

deltaHelpers.text: `diff`, `merge`, `apply`: pure functions; numbers add, arrays union
deltaHelpers.note: Storage does not replicate through them, and `merge({ hits: 10 }, diff({ hits: 10 }, { hits: 3 }))` is 13: a delta is not a plain patch.

meta.text: `meta`: per-field `[ts, origin]`, reset stamp, tombstone, counters, sets, `v`

delete.text: tombstone with empty data; a newer write revives the record
delete.detail: The op log keeps earlier payloads until retention drops them or `purge()` scrubs them (checked by running).

documentObjects.text: `record(id)`: one live, editable `Record` per id, refreshed on any change

identity.text: one `Record` per id while referenced (WeakRef); `get()` returns new copies

returnedData.text: JSON copies in and out; editing them changes nothing
returnedData.detail: `getCachedData()` and `snapshot()` hand out the raw objects on purpose.

relations.text: a `Record` turns any string equal to a known id into a `Reference`
relations.note: Nothing declares the relation, so an unrelated string that matches an id becomes a `Reference` too (checked by running).

contracts.text: `@alexify/syncom/contracts`: arrow functions stored in the chain, run by `new Function`
contracts.note: Load contracts only from a chain you control; the parser takes a single arrow function, and the result is written with `saveData()`.

queryBuilder.text: cursor chains `order()`, `desc()`, `limit()`, `offset()`, `filter()`, `projection()`; the predicate is JSON only

opComparison.text: all six; `$gt`…`$lte` hold only within one kind (number, string, boolean)
opComparison.detail: `{ priority: { $gt: '2' } }` over numbers matches nothing (verified). On an array field, any element may match.

opArray.text: a scalar matches any element; no `$elemMatch`, no `$size` (`filter()` instead)

opRegex.text: `RegExp` or source string, `$options` flags; 1000 characters at most; `g`/`y` dropped

opLogical.text: `$and`, `$or`, and `$not` over a whole query; no `$nor`, no field-level `$not`
opLogical.detail: `$nor: [a, b]` is written `$not: { $or: [a, b] }`; `{ f: { $not: { $gt: 5 } } }` is `$not: { f: { $gt: 5 } }`. A field-level `$not` is `unknown operator` (verified).

jsPredicate.text: `filter(fn)` over the loaded row, applied before `limit()`

dottedPaths.text: in queries, `order()`, `projection()`, `index` and `search`; `items.0.n` reaches into arrays

queryValidation.text: unknown operator or bad argument: `TypeError` at `select()`; field names are not checked
queryValidation.detail: A misspelled field matches nothing, silently (verified).

immutableQueries.text: builders change the cursor in place (`one()` leaves it as it was)

docMatch.text: the compiled predicate is internal (`compileQuery` is not exported)

sort.text: `order()`/`desc()`: several keys, any field, dotted; stable
sort.detail: Order: absent/null, booleans, numbers, strings; arrays and objects keep their place. With no `order()`, rows come in id order, or `$text` rank.

sortIndex.text: no sorted index: every candidate is read, then ordered
sortIndex.detail: Except a covered cursor (order and projection on indexed fields), ordered from the catalog with no record read. Verified: `order('a').limit(2)` read 40 of 40 records; with `projection(['a'])`, 0.

topK.text: `TopK` keeps the best `offset + limit` rows as candidates stream by

skipLimit.text: `offset(n)`, `limit(n)`; an unordered cursor stops reading at enough matches
skipLimit.detail: Verified: an unordered `limit(2)` over 50 records read 2.

streaming.text: `for await` yields an already fetched array; keyset paging by hand

count.text: `count(query)` for any query; from the catalog alone when every field is indexed
count.detail: Verified: an indexed range count read 0 records; any other count reads the candidates. `limit`/`offset` are ignored.

findById.text: `get(id)` (a copy), `record(id)` (a live Record); `hasRecord(id)`; a collection's `get` only its own

findByIds.text: no batch get; `select({ id: { $in } })` reads the whole collection
findByIds.detail: `id` is not posted in the catalog; verified 39 of 40 records read for three ids.

projection.text: `projection(fields)`; answered from the catalog when they are indexed

resultObjects.text: plain JSON copies `{ id, ...data }`, the lens applied; new objects per `fetch()`
resultObjects.detail: A cursor does not run `beforeRead`/`afterRead`; `get(id)` does.

joins.text: a cursor reads one collection; `Reference.record()` follows one id

encryptedFields.text: an `{ encrypted: true }` record is listed, never a query row

secondaryIndexes.text: entity `index: ['field', …]`, or read off a metaschema schema

indexKind.text: equality posting lists; ranges, prefixes and sorts do not use them
indexKind.note: A range or an `order()` on an indexed field is evaluated over every candidate: the whole collection unless an indexed equality or `$in` narrows it. Checked on 200 records: `$gt` read 200, with an indexed equality 20, a covered cursor 0.

compoundIndexes.text: only for `unique` keys; queries intersect single-field postings

arrayIndexes.text: an indexed array is posted under each element

indexValues.text: any JSON value, keyed canonically (object keys in any order)
indexValues.detail: Objects are keyed by key order: `{ meta: { $eq: { b: 2, a: 1 } } }` on an indexed field finds 0 of a record stored as `{ a: 1, b: 2 }`, where the unindexed path finds it (verified).

indexStorage.text: in memory (the catalog), saved to `index/catalog.json`, caught up from the log at open
indexStorage.detail: Every live id, its indexed values and its search text must fit in memory; a first open, a stamp the log cannot resume from, or other indexes rebuild it from one scan of data/.

indexChange.text: edit `index`; the catalog rebuilds once at the next open

planner.text: indexed equalities narrow the candidates before any record is read

indexCombination.text: postings intersect over `$and`, union over an `$or` whose branches are all indexed
indexCombination.detail: Verified: `$or: [{ a }, { b }]` read 9 of 40 records; an `$or` with an unindexed branch reads all.

coveredQueries.text: query, order and projection all indexed: answered from the catalog, no record read

explain.text: no explain API; the plan is private to the cursor

queryCache.text: none; each `fetch()` re-runs, records come from the bounded entry cache

unique.text: `unique` fields and composites; a local write is refused, a peer's clash is a `conflict` event
unique.detail: Verified: a duplicate `slug` and a duplicate `[org, name]` are `VALIDATION_FAILED`. Across peers both records are kept.

fulltext.detail: Diacritics and case folded; ranked best first; postings in memory, rebuilt at open from the text kept in catalog.json; no phrases or boolean text operators; a custom `TextIndex` can replace it.

liveQueries.text: `cursor.watch(listener)`: runs now, then after every change to the collection
liveQueries.detail: Changes that land while a run is in flight coalesce into one more run; a peer's batch is one run. No time-based throttle.

liveIncremental.text: every wake re-runs the whole cursor

liveDistinct.text: the listener runs after any change to the collection, same rows or not
liveDistinct.detail: Verified: updating a record outside the result called the listener with the same rows.

collectionStream.text: storage-wide `change` event `(op, via)`; no per-collection stream
collectionStream.detail: A `set`, `inc` or `delete` op names the record id, not its collection; the listener looks the record up.

documentObservable.text: a live `Record` emits `update (data, delta)`, `null` once deleted

reactivityPrimitive.text: callbacks and events; no observable or signal adapter

liveRemote.text: a peer's ops and snapshot pages wake `watch()`; a batch is one run

replModel.text: operation log; version vectors per origin and scope; pages of ops

wire.text: ops as positional `packOps` arrays, signed; a `set` carries only its delta
wire.detail: About 190 bytes of signature fields per op (docs/guide/sync.md#signatures). A bootstrap snapshot is the exception: whole records with their merge metadata.

replHistory.text: every retained op travels, intermediate writes included
replHistory.detail: Past `retention.ops` (default 10 000) the oldest sealed segments go; a peer the log no longer covers bootstraps from a snapshot.

protocolVersion.text: `PROTOCOL` 1 in `hello`; another version is refused with 400
protocolVersion.detail: The 17 `packOps` slots are appended, never reordered; a reader of fewer slots ignores the rest (CLAUDE.md).

schemaHandshake.text: `hello` swaps `{ version, hash }`; same version, other hash emits `schema` drift
schemaHandshake.detail: A different version is not refused: every op carries `v`, older records are lensed, newer ops applied or held (`ahead`).

foreignBackend.text: none: the far end must be a syncom node hosting `unit()`

customTransport.detail: The link only carries the four procedures; the far end still runs syncom.

roundTrips.text: `hello`, then one `push` per 500 ops, then one `changes` subscription
roundTrips.detail: Live, ops landing in one tick go as one push and the host streams pages on the subscription. A bootstrap adds one `snapshot` call per 500 records.

collectionsPerLink.text: one link carries every collection of the storage, filtered by scope

replMeta.text: a cursor per peer, the version vector, the op log within retention

topology.text: mesh: any node dials and hosts; hubs dial each other

multiMaster.text: any node hosts `unit()`; peers dial each other directly

relay.text: ops relayed hop by hop; the version vector drops what a node has
relay.detail: An op reaches a node at most once per link (docs/guide/sync.md#protocol).

browserHosts.text: `unit()` on a wrpc `PeerHost` over a data channel

scaleOut.text: hubs dial each other; a client stays on one hub's log
scaleOut.detail: A client moved to another hub bootstraps from it. A log shared by hub processes on a broker is reserved: `open({ sync: { sharedLog } })` throws in this version (src/sync.js:98-101).

webrtc.detail: The tests run over a fake data-channel pair at the raw-channel level; a full `WrpcPeer` needs an RTC adapter and is checked by hand (CLAUDE.md). wrpc fragments every message to 16 KiB, or to the negotiated `maxMessageSize` (@alexify/wrpc@2.0.1 src/webrtc/framing.js).

signaling.text: wrpc's `createSignalingUnit` on your hub, or a channel you negotiated

p2pRoom.text: one link per pair you add (`peer.join(room)` + `addNode`); ops relay any path

http.text: no request–response sync; wrpc's SSE transport untested in the repo
http.note: In a one-off check over wrpc 2.0.1, `transport: 'sse'` synced both ways with a live update; plain `http` cannot (the subscription is refused, then every call answers 428).

nats.detail: wrpc has a NATS broker transport; syncom does not use it (the shared-log hub mode is reserved).

conflictDetect.text: no compare step: every op merges by its field's kind

conflictResolve.text: built in: per-field LWW by `(ts, origin)`, per-origin counter sums, OR-sets

customMerge.text: none: the rules are fixed; `beforeApply` can only skip an op

conflictWhere.text: on every node, by the same deterministic rules

conflictEvents.text: unique-key clashes only (`conflict`); a lost concurrent write is silent

causality.text: version vectors for delivery; per-field stamps; no causal context per record
causality.detail: Hence the documented counter-reset case that does not converge as expected.

clocks.text: decide concurrent register writes; a clock never falls behind what it saw
clocks.detail: Skew changes who wins, never whether replicas agree; `maxSkew` (24 h) refuses stamps far ahead.

live.text: built in: the host's `changes` subscription pushes ops as they land

resume.text: the link resumes the subscription from its last event id; push by vector

restart.text: cursor, remote identity and vector are on disk; no bootstrap

reconnect.text: the link's: wrpc reconnects with backoff and a heartbeat; syncom greets again

retry.text: a failed push leaves the peer `behind`, caught up later; backoff 1 s to 60 s
retry.detail: A page that fails to apply is retried from the saved cursor; three failures in a row leave the peer `stuck` (src/sync.js:616-634).

dup.text: duplicates dropped by the vector; an op ahead of its stream dropped as a gap
dup.detail: docs/guide/sync.md:173-174 says such an op "is set aside until the ones before it arrive"; the code drops it, counts `gaps`, and it lands only when sent again.

offline.text: own ops kept until the registered nodes hold them; pushed when a peer is back
offline.note: Ops written before any node was registered, and compacted since, cannot reach a host; it is reported once per hello (`UNDELIVERABLE`).
offline.detail: scratchpad/replication/verify/syncom-offline-retention.js: retention 50, 300 offline inserts → the host holds 0 records, and a later write does not land either; the dialer reports no error.

bootstrap.text: replays the host's log, or past its retention a streamed snapshot
bootstrap.detail: Snapshot records carry their merge metadata, arrive as NDJSON over a wrpc binary stream, and join as `merge` ops, so a bootstrap is transitive.

longOffline.text: a snapshot of its scopes once the host's log no longer covers it

batch.text: `pageSize` 500 ops per push and per page; 500 records per snapshot page
batch.detail: `pageBytes` (4 MiB): a snapshot page above it is sent inline rather than streamed.

flow.text: per-peer outbox capped (`maxOutbox` 10 000); pages applied one at a time
flow.detail: Beyond the cap the backlog is dropped and the peer recovers from the vector. Snapshot pages stream with wrpc backpressure.

partial.text: per-record scopes; the host bounds a peer's reads and writes by the record's scope
partial.detail: src/commit.js:110-115 computes the scope from `payload.data` (the delta of a `set`). scratchpad/replication/verify/syncom-scope-of-set2.js: a peer granted only `Other` receives `{ title: "secret v2" }` of a `Doc` record. scratchpad/replication/verify/syncom-scope-write.js: the same peer overwrites the host's `Doc` record. tests/suites/sync-engine.js:327-350 covers inserts only.

partialLive.text: one subscription serves the granted scopes; other scopes' ops are skipped

revoke.text: no revocation: the peer keeps what it received

oneWay.text: every link pushes and subscribes; scopes bound both directions alike

deletes.text: a `delete` op leaves a tombstone on every node; a `purge` op erases
deletes.detail: Tombstones are never cleaned up, so a long-offline peer cannot resurrect a record by absence; a newer write revives it by stamp.

replAttachments.text: none: records are JSON, with no binary type

lifecycle.text: `sync.start()`/`stop()` for all peers; `enableNode(url, false)` per peer

awaitSync.text: `sync(url?)` resolves once pushed; nothing awaits the inbound side
awaitSync.detail: `storage.sync.toPromise('sync')` resolves on the next push or received page.

resync.text: `sync()` pushes what peers lack; `enableNode` off and on greets again

status.text: `peers()`: connected, cursor, pending, behind, stuck, lastError; `hosted()`; events
status.detail: Events `peer`, `sync`, `bootstrap`, `error`, `refused`, `hello`, `node`; storage `change` and `apply`; OpenTelemetry spans and a replication-lag metric.

replMultiTab.text: one tab owns the storage and its sync; others get `LOCKED` or wait
replMultiTab.detail: A SharedWorker can share wrpc's connection (`WrpcClientProxy`), not the storage; a storage served from a worker is the planned follow-up.

serverProduct.text: `sync.unit()`: four procedures for any wrpc router, in the same MIT package

serverRuntime.text: wherever a wrpc router runs: Node servers, a browser `PeerHost`

adapters.detail: syncom's own tests run on wrpc's `Server` only (tests/wrpc.integration.test.js:37-44).

remoteQuery.text: none: a client replicates its scopes and queries locally

serverStorage.text: a full syncom node: its own log and records over its `fsi`

atRest.text: per record (`{ encrypted: true }`) or the whole storage; such records never sync
atRest.note: The RSA key pair that unseals the records sits unprotected in `<path>/keys/`, beside the data: whoever can read the directory can read the records.

encScope.text: the record's whole data; its id, collection and timestamps stay readable
encScope.detail: Checked by running: the record file is `{ data: <envelope>, meta: null, encrypted: true, timestamp, block }`; the file name is the id, the catalog row keeps `$type`, the chain block keeps the ciphertext's hash.

cipher.text: AES-256-GCM with a fresh key per record, wrapped by RSA-OAEP-256
cipher.detail: The same envelope on Node.js and in the browser, so ciphertext and keys move between them; an unknown envelope version is `BAD_ENVELOPE`.

keyOffDisk.text: the RSA private key is a file in `<path>/keys/`, beside the data
keyOffDisk.note: Mode 0600 where the backend has permissions; in OPFS or IndexedDB a plain entry. No passphrase, KMS or injected key.

keyRotation.text: no rotation API; a replaced key pair cannot open sealed records

encExport.text: no backup or export API; `snapshot()` leaves encrypted records out
encExport.detail: A copy of the directory keeps the ciphertext, and `keys/` with it.

encSync.text: encrypted records stay local: no op, no snapshot, no peer copy

e2ee.text: recipe: seal fields in `beforeWrite`, open in `afterRead` (wrpc's HPKE sealer)
e2ee.note: One paragraph, with no example or test in the repository; a sealed field cannot be indexed, queried, counted or kept unique.

signing.text: Ed25519 per op: the header plus a salted payload digest
signing.note: The default `'verify'` takes an unsigned op, so a relay can strip signatures; only `sync.signatures: 'require'` refuses them.

nodeIdentity.text: the node id is its Ed25519 public key; a swapped key is `IDENTITY_MISMATCH`

tamper.text: hash-linked chain of what this node applied, unsigned (optional)
tamper.note: Whoever can write the directory can rebuild it: a read checks a record against the block its file names, not that the block is on the chain, so a planted block passes and `validate()` still answers true (checked). The ops in the log are what is signed.
tamper.detail: Script: change a record's data, write a block `{ prev: '0', data: { id, hash } }` under its own hash, point the record at it: `get()` returns the forged data. `chain: false` keeps no chain.

authn.text: `unit({ authorize })` gates `hello`; `access: 'session'` refuses everyone by default
authn.note: `hello` does not prove the peer holds its key, and the dialer's `token` sits in plain text in `<path>/remote/`.

peerValidation.text: host `authorize`; dialer `beforeConnect`, `beforeBootstrap`; key possession not proven
peerValidation.detail: Under `'require'` a host refuses a `hello` whose node id is no key (403 `UNSIGNED`); a peer greeting with someone else's key then fails every push as `forged`.

access.text: per-record scopes (`sync.scope`); a peer reads only the scopes `hello` granted
access.note: The peer names its scopes, and naming none means everything: `authorize` must check `hello.scopes`.

writeRules.text: ops outside granted scopes refused, by the op's scope and its record's; `beforeApply({ op, peer })` can skip one
writeRules.note: A finer rule than scopes lives in `beforeApply`: a skip is local (the op is still logged and relayed), a throw refuses the whole page.

serverValidation.text: the host runs the entity validators on every peer op (`OP_INVALID`)
serverValidation.detail: A peer's op is never rewritten by the validator: the verdict alone decides, and an invalid op is skipped and reported (see the next row for where it goes).

serverAuth.text: out-of-scope (by the op or its record), unsigned and malformed ops stop at the host; one its validator or `beforeApply` skips is relayed
serverAuth.note: Checked with three nodes: an op the middle node's validator or `beforeApply` skipped still reached the node behind it, because a withheld op would leave a gap in its origin's stream; every node re-checks it. A throwing `beforeApply` refuses the whole page instead, and the sender offers it again later.

purge.text: `purge(id)`: a `purge` op that wins at any stamp, then a scrub of the op log
purge.note: The chain keeps an unsalted SHA-256 of every version this node wrote or applied, so whoever holds the directory can confirm a guessed record; until the next catalog save, `index/catalog.json` may still hold its indexed fields.
purge.detail: A scrub rewrites log files in place: a crash mid-scrub tears the file, and `purge()` is idempotent. The scrubbed op keeps origin, seq, stamp, `actor`, `sig` and the salted digest.

purgeReplicas.text: the purge op replicates; every peer that takes it scrubs its own log
purgeReplicas.note: A peer that never comes back keeps what it had.

history.text: `history(id)`, `get(id, { at })`, `diff`/`restore`, tags of the whole storage
history.detail: A version is a fold of the retained log: exact from the last whole-record write above what retention dropped, otherwise `HISTORY_GONE`. `retention.ops` defaults to 10 000; a tag keeps the whole storage as it was, copy-on-write.

audit.text: every op names its origin key and an `actor`, kept in the log
audit.note: `actor` is the writer's signed claim; a host holds it to what `authorize` established in `beforeApply`.

proto.text: own keys only; `__proto__` is never a field
proto.detail: Checked by running: `insert`, `update` and `applyRemote` with own `__proto__` keys left `Object.prototype` clean; the key is dropped.

malformed.text: `wellFormed` before anything is read; counted `malformed`, never logged or relayed
malformed.detail: Checked by running: an origin with `@`, an id with `../` and a stamp three days ahead were all counted malformed; payloads are `applyOp`'s and taken as no-ops when garbage.

skew.text: stamps over `sync.maxSkew` (24 h) ahead refused (`SKEW`), never observed

hooks.text: `beforeWrite` replaces data or refuses, `afterWrite`; one function per name
hooks.detail: Run inside the mutation queue for every local write (`write`, `set`, `inc`, `add`, `remove`, `delete`, `purge`, `merge`); a write issued from a hook is refused (`IN_HOOK`); an unknown hook name is a `TypeError` at `open()`.

replHooks.detail: A peer's op is judged, never rewritten.

outHook.text: none, by design: a withheld op is a gap; scopes decide what leaves

readHooks.text: `beforeRead` / `afterRead` wrap `get()`; queries and snapshots read raw
readHooks.note: An `afterRead` redaction does not reach `select()` rows, so it is not a read access control.

errorEvents.text: `error` with a code per refused peer op; `conflict`; host `refused`, `hello`
errorEvents.detail: Listeners are never awaited; a throwing one is logged (`listener.error`) and an `error` with no listener is silent.

plugins.detail: Subpaths (`/wrpc`, `/contracts`, `/idb`, `/search`) are separate modules, not plugins; nothing is global to the process.

errors.detail: A host's wire refusal is a plain error with wrpc's numeric code (400–429) and a `reason` constant.

logging.text: `open({ logger })`: a Console, a pino-shaped logger or `false`; named events

otel.text: spans and metrics through an injected API; no OpenTelemetry dependency

diagPII.text: no id, origin, scope or key as a metric label; `includeIdentity: false` for spans
diagPII.detail: Log lines name record ids and origins, never payloads; `error` events carry the op as a field.

devMode.text: no separate mode: argument checks and full error messages always on

testing.text: `createMemoryFsi()` for in-memory stores; contract suites stay in the repo
testing.detail: tests/utils/memory-link.js (an in-process link) and tests/utils/mesh.js (N storages, `settle()`) are repo-only.

ci.text: 722 `node:test` tests; coverage gate 95/95/90/95; CI on Node 22 and 24, Linux
ci.source: pnpm test (2026-10-23: 722 tests, 721 pass, 1 skipped); package.json scripts.test:coverage; .github/workflows/ci.yml
ci.detail: Browser halves run under Node with an OPFS mock and fake-indexeddb; no real browser in CI.

docs.text: 21 pages, about 41,500 words, with an API reference
docs.detail: The word count includes the generated comparison table.

examples.text: two Node.js scripts (`examples/main.js`, `domain.js`), linted but not run

breakingMajors.detail: The wire carries `PROTOCOL = 1` and a host refuses another version with 400 `PROTOCOL` (src/protocol.js:8; src/hosting.js:167-168). `packOps` slots are append-only and a new op type is a PROTOCOL bump (CLAUDE.md). The catalog is derived state: a catalog.json of an older format (now 3) is rebuilt once at open (src/catalog.js:25,403; CHANGELOG.md).

releaseCadence.text: no release yet; cut by hand from a checklist

commercialSupport.detail: SECURITY.md promises to acknowledge a vulnerability report within 7 days and a fix or plan within 30.

communityHelp.text: GitHub repository; no chat or forum

importFromOtherDbs.text: no importer and no JSON import; write records with `insert()`

benchmarks.text: nine libraries, nine scenarios, memory and disk; machine and date stated

agentDocs.text: `llms.txt` on the docs site; `CLAUDE.md` in the repository

version.source: npm view rxdb dist-tags time (2026-10-23); rxdb@17.6.0 package.json:4; CHANGELOG.md:11

serverLicense.text: RxServer (`rxdb-server`) is SSPL; its Fastify and Koa adapters are Premium (Pro Plus)
serverLicense.source: rxdb-server package.json:5 and LICENSE (SSPL v1); npm view rxdb-server license; https://rxdb.info/premium/
serverLicense.detail: The Express adapter (rxdb-server src/plugins/adapter-express) is in the SSPL repository; Fastify/Koa adapters are in the Pro Plus tier.

price.text: Premium: Pro from $99/month, Pro Plus from $239/month, billed yearly; Enterprise custom
price.detail: Prices are per organization with unlimited developers; no free trial and no monthly plan (premium FAQ). Upgrades are credited. Enterprise adds a custom MSA, named engineer, SLA and source-code access.

premiumSplit.text: Pro: OPFS, IndexedDB, SQLite, filesystem storages, WebCrypto encryption, fulltext search; Pro Plus: worker, sharding, logger…
premiumSplit.detail: Pro Plus adds the Worker and SharedWorker storages, Sharding, Memory-Mapped, the Localstorage Meta Optimizer, the Query Optimizer, the RxServer Fastify/Koa adapters and the logger plugin. The free tier's list strikes through 'Premium storages (OPFS, SQLite, Filesystem)' and 'Performance plugins (Sharding, Memory Mapped)'; the extracted page text loses the strike-through. The same list still names a free LokiJS storage, removed in 16.0.0. 17.0.0 moved reactivity-vue and reactivity-preact-signals from Premium into the core.

premiumTerms.text: yearly term license: use must stop when it lapses; not inside a library
premiumTerms.source: https://rxdb.info/license-preview/ (same text in rxdb@17.6.0 docs-src/src/pages/license-preview.tsx:63,71,111,120-126,159-165); npm view rxdb-premium scripts
premiumTerms.note: The agreement also requires shipping Premium code minified without source maps, gives no technical support, and says installing it (an access-token `postinstall` downloads and decrypts it) sends the package name, dependency list, git user name and email, and IP address to the vendor.
premiumTerms.detail: Continued use of an already deployed release after expiry is a paid add-on option; the license auto-renews yearly; governed by German law (Stuttgart). The public `rxdb-premium` npm package is 3 files (11.9 KB) whose postinstall runs scripts/installer.js.

collectionLimit.text: free core: 13 open collections per JavaScript process; Premium lifts it
collectionLimit.note: Measured: the 14th collection opens after a wait of about 1.86 s and the 15th throws `COL23`. The count spans every database in the process; 17.0.0 lowered it from 16 to 13.
collectionLimit.detail: The wait is a retry loop (60 × 30 ms) meant for test suites that close databases without awaiting; the throw only fires when more than 13 are open after it. Removing it needs `setPremiumFlag()` from rxdb-premium (a SHA-256-checked flag); the source comment says forking to remove it is allowed.

phoneHome.text: dev-mode loads a hidden rxdb.info iframe; WebRTC defaults to `signaling.rxdb.info`; Premium install reports to the vendor
phoneHome.note: The docs say the dev-mode iframe is added on localhost only, but the `isLocalHost()` check is commented out (`dev-mode-tracking.ts:67`), so it loads on any host unless the Premium flag is set. The production core makes no such call.
phoneHome.detail: The iframe is https://rxdb.info/html/dev-mode-iframe.html?version=<RXDB_VERSION>, 1×1 px, 'to track the results of marketing efforts'. The free Dexie and SQLite-trial storages also print a Premium advert with console.warn on their first write, in production too (rx-storage-instance-dexie.ts:83-100; sqlite-storage-instance.ts:138-155).

deps.text: 24 direct plus the required peer `rxjs`: 74 packages installed
deps.detail: Counted from the lockfile: 72 packages are reached from rxdb's 24 dependencies, 74 with rxjs and its tslib. They include graphql, graphql-ws, simple-peer, nostr-tools, ws, dexie, crypto-js and three schema validators (ajv, z-schema, is-my-json-valid), installed whether or not the plugins are used; `as-typed`, `@types/ws` and `@types/simple-peer` (pulling `@types/node`) are runtime dependencies used only for types. Optional peers: react, vue, @angular/core, @preact/signals-core, firebase, mongodb, nats.

impl.text: TypeScript, built by Babel into CommonJS and ESM; `sideEffects: false`
impl.source: rxdb@17.6.0 package.json:88-98; package.json scripts build:cjs, build:esm, build:types; babel.config.js
impl.detail: The CJS build lowers classes (ES5 target); the ESM build keeps them. The npm package also ships `src/` (TypeScript), CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and ERROR-MESSAGES.md.

types.text: generated from the source; document type inferred from the schema
types.detail: 17.0.0 typed the `$$` signal accessors with the document type (HKT-based ReactivityLambda).

size.text: 80.4 KB min+gzip: `createRxDatabase` with Dexie; 44.9 KB with localStorage
size.source: esbuild 0.28.2, minified browser ESM, from bench/compare/node_modules (scratch size.js, size2.js); rxdb master config/bundle-size/limits.json
size.detail: Core + memory 45.2 KB; core + Dexie 78.7 KB with the `es2015` condition for rxjs (https://rxdb.info/install.html); + `wrappedValidateAjvStorage` (needed by dev-mode) 121.2 KB. Master's new size check caps its todo-dexie app at 84,671 B gzip, consistent with these numbers.

sizeSync.detail: With localStorage instead of Dexie: 57.9 KB (scratch size2.js). size.json labels the bundle dexie@4.4.6, but esbuild resolved rxdb's own pinned dexie@4.4.2 (size.js:137-139 reads the version from the top-level node_modules).

sizeGate.text: CI prints a webpack build size; no limit in 17.6.0
sizeGate.detail: Master adds an esbuild check with limits (orga/changelog/add-bundle-size-ci-check.json; config/bundle-size/limits.json), unreleased.

node.text: ≥20; free disk persistence only via MongoDB or FoundationDB servers, or the capped SQLite trial
node.note: The Filesystem and SQLite storages are Premium (Pro); the free SQLite trial stops at 500 documents and after 500 SQL calls per storage instance.
node.detail: CI runs Node 26.10.0 (.nvmrc) on Linux and Windows; the `engines` floor of 20 is not exercised in CI. The memory storage is free.

deno.text: `rxdb/plugins/storage-denokv`; CI runs the Dexie and DenoKV suites on Deno 2.6.5

bun.text: CI runs the memory-storage suite on Bun 1.4.2; no Bun-specific storage

browser.text: free: Dexie (IndexedDB), localStorage, memory; native IndexedDB and OPFS Premium (Pro)
browser.source: rxdb@17.6.0 src/plugins/storage-dexie, storage-localstorage, storage-memory; https://rxdb.info/install.html#storages; https://rxdb.info/premium/

browserReq.text: `crypto.subtle` (secure context) or your own `hashFunction`; some bundlers need a `global` shim

worker.text: Worker and SharedWorker storages are Premium (Pro Plus); the free core runs inside a worker
worker.detail: The free `rxdb/plugins/storage-remote` with a custom `messageChannelCreator` is the building block the Premium worker storage uses (https://rxdb.info/rx-storage-remote.html).

reactNative.text: Premium SQLite or Expo Filesystem storage; the free SQLite trial is capped
reactNative.note: The page offers SQLite as 'a free solution' but its sample imports `rxdb-premium/plugins/storage-sqlite`, and the sample's `ignoreDuplicate: true` throws `DB9` without dev-mode (checked).
reactNative.detail: The CI-tested Expo example uses the SQLite trial and shims `crypto.subtle` with expo-crypto (examples/react-native/initializeDb.js:27-29). The React hooks work unchanged in React Native (https://rxdb.info/react.html#react-native-compatibility).

expo.text: Expo Filesystem storage is Premium (Pro); free: expo-sqlite through the SQLite trial

capacitor.text: Premium SQLite via `@capacitor-community/sqlite`; free: localStorage or Dexie in the WebView

electron.text: `rxdb/plugins/electron`: storage in the main process, databases in renderers over IPC
electron.detail: The docs recommend the Premium SQLite storage in the main process and require `nodeIntegration`; the CI example uses the SQLite trial.

tauri.text: SQLite storage with `getSQLiteBasicsTauri()`: Premium, or the capped free trial

flutter.text: `rxdb/plugins/flutter` runs RxDB in QuickJS; its recipe needs the removed LokiJS storage
flutter.note: The article and examples/flutter import `rxdb/plugins/storage-lokijs`, removed in 16.0.0; the Flutter CI job is commented out, and the Dart package on pub.dev is 15.0.0-beta.31 from 2023-11-21.
flutter.detail: Sources: examples/flutter/javascript/src/index.js:5-6; .github/workflows/main.yml:899-945; https://rxdb.info/releases/16.0.0.html; pub.dev/api/packages/rxdb (2026-10-23). The article also says the Dart package is not on pub.dev.

multiTab.text: `multiInstance: true` (default): every tab opens it; changes cross over BroadcastChannel
multiTab.detail: Dexie, SQLite and DenoKV storages broadcast through the broadcast-channel package (native BroadcastChannel, else IndexedDB or localStorage; Unix sockets between Node.js processes); the localStorage storage listens to the `storage` event; the memory storage is per tab. Replications start only in the leader tab by default (`waitForLeadership: true`, src/plugins/replication/index.ts:794, 873).

storageContract.detail: The storage owns persistence, indexes, query execution, revision-conflict detection (`previous` vs stored `_rev`), attachments and tombstone cleanup. Each document write is atomic; there is no transaction around a batch (rx-storage.interface.d.ts:155-163).

customBackend.text: implement `RxStorageInstance`; the storage suite runs from a clone of the repo
customBackend.detail: No docs page explains writing a storage. custom-storage.ts says to clone the repo, export an `RxTestStorage` and run the unit suite with DEFAULT_STORAGE=custom (rx-storage-implementations.test.ts is 3,869 lines, rx-storage-query-correctness.test.ts 2,539). Helpers ship: `categorizeBulkWriteRows`, `getQueryMatcher`, `getSortComparator`, `addRxStorageMultiInstanceSupport`.

memoryBackend.text: `storage-memory` (free): plain objects, binary-search indexes; Node and browser
memoryBackend.detail: State lives in a module-level Map that survives close() for the life of the process, so two databases of one name share it (tests simulate tabs this way). Supports attachments.

indexeddb.note: The free Dexie storage prints a console warning advertising Premium once per process, when a database is created, unless the Premium package's `setPremiumFlag()` is called; it also refuses indexes on fields that are not required (`DXE1`).
indexeddb.detail: Browser; in Node only through fake-indexeddb (in memory). The Dexie page says Premium IndexedDB stores attachments as binary instead of base64, but in 17.6.0 the Dexie storage also stores attachment Blobs (rx-storage-instance-dexie.ts:185-201). Premium IndexedDB's batched cursor, custom index strings, WAL-like mode and Storage Buckets support are from the docs (closed source, not checked).

opfs.text: Premium (Pro) `storage-opfs`: in a worker (sync handles) or `getRxStorageOPFSMainThread()`
opfs.detail: The worker variant is opened through `getRxStorageWorker` and a prebuilt opfs.worker.js; the premium page lists the Worker storage under Pro Plus and does not say whether Pro covers this use. rx-storage.html imports `getRxStorageOPFSMainThread` from storage-worker, rx-storage-opfs.html from storage-opfs. No OPFS code or trial in the open-source package.

localStorage.text: `storage-localstorage` (free): a key per document, a JSON array per index; browser
localStorage.detail: The docs' recommended starting storage. ~5 MB per origin; not available in workers; in Node only with `getLocalStorageMock()` (in memory). No transactions: documents are written before the index keys, each index array rewritten whole on every write. Attachments are stored as base64 data URLs.

nodeFs.detail: Per the docs: plain JSON/txt files, several processes on one folder with `multiInstance: true`. Closed source, not checked. The free persistent options in Node are the MongoDB and FoundationDB servers and the SQLite trial.

sqlite.note: The trial throws `SQL3` after 500 SQL calls per storage instance: a write runs one whole-table read plus one insert per new document, so the 251st serial insert fails (measured). `SQL2` stops it at 500 documents. It has no indexes or attachments.
sqlite.detail: Measured with rxdb 17.6.0 and node:sqlite (scratch script): one bulkInsert of 400 documents passes, 499 throws SQL3. `setPremiumFlag()` only silences the trial's log; the caps are not gated on it (lines 138-157 vs 116, 242). Premium `sqliteBasics` adapters: sqlite3, node:sqlite, wa-sqlite (browser), react-native-quick-sqlite, expo-sqlite, Capacitor, Tauri.

mongodbStorage.note: One Node.js process per MongoDB database, per the docs; nothing in the storage enforces it (no change-stream listening, a TODO in the code).
mongodbStorage.detail: Writes from outside RxDB are not supported. master fixes `findDocumentsById` when `_id` is the primary key (orga/changelog/fix-mongodb-find-by-id-with-_id-primary-key.json).

foundationdb.text: `storage-foundationdb` (free), Node with the native client; one process per cluster

denokv.note: Attachments are not implemented (`getAttachmentData()` throws "Method not implemented."); the DenoKV page does not say so.

legacyStorages.text: removed: PouchDB in 14.0.0; LokiJS and memory-synced in 16.0.0
legacyStorages.note: The premium page still lists LokiJS among the free default storages.
legacyStorages.source: https://rxdb.info/releases/14.0.0.html; https://rxdb.info/releases/16.0.0.html; https://rxdb.info/rx-storage-lokijs.html; rxdb master docs-src/src/pages/premium.tsx:148

storageTrialLimits.text: SQLite trial capped; Dexie prints a Premium notice; no trial of other Premium storages
storageTrialLimits.detail: The 13-open-collections limit of the open-source core is the platform area's row.

storageWrappers.text: `wrapRxStorageInstance`: validation, key compression, encryption, attachment compression stack
storageWrappers.detail: A base storage refuses a schema with `keyCompression`, encryption or attachment compression unless the matching wrapper sits above it (`UT5`–`UT7`).

remoteStorage.text: `storage-remote` over any message channel; `storage-remote-websocket`; Electron IPC
remoteStorage.detail: All free. Both ends must run the same RxDB version (`RM1`).

sharding.detail: Changing `shards` on existing data loses access to it, per the docs.

memoryMapped.note: By default a write resolves before it reaches the persistent storage (`awaitWritePersistence: true` waits); no attachments; one JavaScript process per store, a SharedWorker for tabs.

openCost.text: lazy per collection; Premium (Pro Plus) meta optimizer keeps internal metadata in localStorage
openCost.detail: The docs claim about 200 ms saved on first load with more than four collections; browser only.

durability.text: the storage's job; contract: each document atomic, no batch transaction
durability.detail: Dexie runs a bulkWrite in one IndexedDB readwrite transaction; localStorage has none (the code says so); memory-mapped acknowledges before persisting unless `awaitWritePersistence`; Premium IndexedDB is 'WAL-like' per its docs.

crashRecovery.text: the storage engine's own (IndexedDB, SQLite transactions); no replay in the core
crashRecovery.detail: Semi-persistent storages (memory-mapped) can lose writes not yet persisted when the process dies.

exclusiveOpen.text: no lock: tabs and processes share a store (`multiInstance`); single-process storages unguarded
exclusiveOpen.detail: Change events cross instances over BroadcastChannel and concurrent writes conflict on `_rev`; a second database of the same name in one process throws `DB8` (unless `ignoreDuplicate`/`closeDuplicates`). MongoDB, FoundationDB and memory-mapped need a single process, per their docs.

integrityRepair.text: none; attachment digests serve change detection only
integrityRepair.source: rxdb@17.6.0 src/plugins/attachments-compression/index.ts:170-176 ("RxDB does not use digests for integrity verification")

quotas.text: none in the core; the storage's `QuotaExceededError` reaches the caller
quotas.detail: The IndexedDB-limits article tells the app to catch QuotaExceededError and call navigator.storage.persist(); compression plugins reduce size; Premium IndexedDB accepts Storage Buckets.

onDiskFormat.text: per storage: JSON documents with `_rev`, `_meta` (Dexie, localStorage, SQLite, MongoDB); Premium formats undocumented
onDiskFormat.detail: Memory-mapped writes 'blockchain-like' blocks, so moving to it needs `migrateStorage()`; the filesystem-node docs say plain JSON/txt files. Data is laid out per schema version (table or key `<collection>-<version>`).

writeFootprint.text: one document row per write, plus the storage's index entries
writeFootprint.detail: Measured with storage-localstorage: the same record is a 144-byte document; each index is one JSON array rewritten on every write.

compression.detail: Key compression needs `keyCompression: true` in the schema plus the wrapper; jsonschema-key-compression (ISC, 1.7.0) reports ~40% on its example. Attachment compression is MIME-aware and uses CompressionStream.

docCache.text: `DocumentCache` per collection: RxDocuments by revision, held by WeakRef
docCache.detail: The query cache belongs to the query area.

attachments.note: Not supported by the SQLite trial (`SQL1`), MongoDB, DenoKV or memory-mapped storages.

localDocs.detail: Opt-in per database or collection (`localDocuments: true`); ids up to 128 characters; no attachments.

tombstoneCleanup.text: `cleanup` plugin: purges tombstones after 31 days, once replications are in sync
tombstoneCleanup.detail: Without the plugin tombstones stay; runs on the leader only by default; `collection.cleanup(0)` purges now.

storageMigration.text: `migrateStorage()` (free): moves live documents batch by batch into a new database
storageMigration.note: It deletes each migrated batch from the old storage and does not check write errors on the new one (a TODO in the code); deleted documents are dropped.

backup.text: `backup` plugin: Node only, one-time or live, a `document.json` per document; no restore

jsonDump.note: A dump has no deleted documents and no revisions, holds encrypted fields in plain text, and is built in memory.

model.text: JSON documents; every collection has a JSON Schema

schemaless.text: schema required; an open `type: 'object'` sub-field, RxState or local docs
schemaless.source: https://rxdb.info/rx-schema.html (FAQ: How to store schemaless data?); rxdb@17.6.0 src/rx-schema-helper.ts:204

collectionNames.text: never shadows database members; regex checked in dev-mode
collectionNames.detail: The docs give `^[a-z][a-z0-9]*$`; the dev-mode check is `^[a-z][_$a-zA-Z0-9\-]*$` plus DB5 for names of RxDatabase members. Without the Premium flag at most 13 (14 after a delay) collections are open per process — see the license row.

fieldNames.text: letters, digits, `_`; no leading `_`; no RxDocument member names
fieldNames.detail: Checked by the dev-mode plugin at schema creation; `_id` and `_deleted` are the allowed underscore names.

primaryKey.text: a top-level string field named by `primaryKey` (`_id` allowed)

compositeKey.text: `primaryKey: { key, fields, separator }`, filled on insert

idGeneration.text: the caller supplies the key; a composite key is derived
idGeneration.detail: Since 10.0 the primary key is mandatory and never generated; the docs' examples use `crypto.randomUUID()`.

idRules.text: string with `maxLength`; values checked only by a validator and dev-mode
idRules.note: Without dev-mode and a validator, an empty, over-long or missing key is accepted; on the memory storage an insert without the key was stored under `undefined` (IndexedDB rejects that one).
idRules.detail: Dev-mode refuses an empty key, leading or trailing whitespace, `\r`, `\n` and `"`; there is no character class otherwise.

immutableFields.text: `final: true`; the primary key is final — enforced in dev-mode only
immutableFields.note: Without dev-mode, `patch()` overwrote a `final` field, and patching the primary key wrote a copy under the new key beside the original (checked by running); dev-mode refuses both (`DOC9`).
immutableFields.detail: The docs say final fields are always required; the code does not add them to `required`, so a final field left out at insert can never be set (DOC9). Patching the primary key in production left the old document and wrote a second one under the new key.

schemaFormat.detail: Top-level `additionalProperties` is forced to `false` (src/rx-schema-helper.ts:204); `$ref` is refused in dev-mode (SC40).

validators.note: The `validate-ajv-standalone` plugin documented on rxdb.info is not in 17.6.0; it is on master, unreleased.
validators.detail: rxdb master orga/changelog/add-validate-ajv-standalone-plugin.json. ajv, ajv-formats and z-schema are runtime dependencies of the rxdb package.

validationDefault.text: off until the storage is wrapped; dev-mode refuses to start without it
validationDefault.note: Without the wrapper, production accepts unknown top-level fields, wrong types and missing required fields (checked by running).

validatorOutput.text: validators return errors only; the data is written as given

checkOnly.text: `getValidator(schema)` from the validate plugin; no collection method

tsInference.text: `ExtractDocumentTypeFromTypedRxJsonSchema` from an `as const` schema; typed collections

defaults.text: `default` on top-level fields, filled by insert and upsert
defaults.detail: Nested defaults are refused in dev-mode (SC7) and ignored otherwise; a migration does not fill them (https://rxdb.info/migration-schema.html, Default values are not auto-applied).

required.text: JSON Schema `required`; the primary key always
required.detail: Enforced only when a validator plugin wraps the storage.

nested.text: nested schemas; dotted paths in update operators and queries
nested.detail: Across replicas the unit is still the document, unless the `crdt` plugin replays `$set` on dotted paths.

schemaVersion.text: `version` per collection; a changed schema without a bump throws `DB6`

migration.text: `migrationStrategies` per version, at open; returning `null` drops a document
migration.detail: Async strategies; `autoMigrate: false` with `startMigration()`/`migratePromise()`; a state observable; one tab runs it (leader election); the replication meta is migrated too.

readOld.detail: Checked by running with `autoMigrate: false`: `find()` returned `[]` and `insert()` threw COL25 until `migratePromise()` finished. By default `addCollections()` waits for the migration.

peerVersions.text: no version on documents; run the same migration on server and clients
peerVersions.detail: The pull checkpoint is not migrated, so the backend must accept checkpoints of older versions. Overlaps the replication area's schema-versions row.

bulk.text: `bulkInsert`, `bulkUpsert`, `bulkRemove` with per-document success and error lists

upsert.detail: The docs say parallel `upsert()` calls throw 409; in 17.6.0 an existing document goes through the incremental write queue, and 20 parallel upserts all succeeded (checked by running).

operators.detail: The typed list is `$min $max $inc $set $unset $push $addToSet $pop $pullAll $rename`; mingo also ran `$pull` (checked by running).

byQuery.detail: One write per matched document, not atomic.

cas.text: every non-incremental write checks `_rev`; a stale one throws 409 `CONFLICT`

localConflicts.text: a stale `patch`/`modify`/`update` throws 409; the `incremental*` methods retry
localConflicts.source: rxdb@17.6.0 src/rx-document.ts:307-364; https://rxdb.info/rx-document.html (Prevent conflicts with the incremental methods)
localConflicts.detail: Checked by running: `patch()` on an outdated RxDocument threw CONFLICT, `incrementalPatch()` on the same instance succeeded.

transactions.text: none; one document write is the atomic unit
transactions.detail: Checked by running: a `bulkInsert` with one duplicate id wrote the other two documents and returned the 409 in `error`.

changeAndDelete.source: https://rxdb.info/rx-document.html (Remove and update in a single atomic operation)

counters.text: `$inc` is local; it converges only under the `crdt` plugin
counters.detail: Without the CRDT plugin a replication conflict keeps one side's document (the default handler keeps the master state). Checked by running: two databases each `$inc` by 1, the CRDT merge gave 2.

sets.text: `$addToSet`/`$pullAll`; `crdt` replays them in creator order, not observed-remove
sets.detail: Checked by running: a remove concurrent with a re-add of the same element kept or dropped it depending on which of the two databases' random storage tokens sorts last.

lists.detail: Concurrent pushes both survive, ordered by creator id (checked by running).

text.source: rxdb@17.6.0 src (no text CRDT); https://rxdb.info/crdt.html (Why not automerge.js or yjs?)

crdtModel.text: opt-in `crdt` plugin per schema; otherwise a conflict handler

mergeGranularity.text: the default handler keeps the master's whole document; merging needs a handler or `crdt`

registerWinner.text: `crdt`: op position, then storage-token order, not time; otherwise the master
registerWinner.detail: Checked by running: two databases each `$set` the same field once; both merge directions kept the value of the database whose random storage token sorts higher.

mergeHistory.text: `crdt`: every op stored inside the document, never compacted
mergeHistory.note: The document grows with every write: 200 `$inc` left 201 op rows, about 18 KB (checked by running), and every replica stores and transfers them.

mergeBypass.text: `modify()` is refused, but `upsert()`/`incrementalUpsert()` replace the op history
mergeBypass.note: Checked by running: `upsert()` over a CRDT document reset its op list to one entry, `incrementalUpsert()` dropped the CRDT field, and with the `update` plugin added after `crdt`, `update()` wrote outside the ops. Dev-mode stops the last two, not `upsert()`.

deltaHelpers.text: none; `mergeCRDTFields` merges the plugin's own field only

meta.detail: The revision token is the writing database's token, not a content hash; replication strips `_rev`.

delete.text: `_deleted: true` with the full data until `cleanup`; re-insert revives
delete.detail: Checked by running: the removed document kept every field with `_deleted: true`; inserting the id again wrote revision 3.

documentObjects.source: rxdb@17.6.0 src/rx-document.ts:95-130; https://rxdb.info/rx-document.html (Document Lifetime and Immutability)

identity.text: one `RxDocument` per revision while referenced (WeakRef cache)
identity.detail: Checked by running: two `findOne().exec()` calls returned the same instance.

returnedData.text: deep-frozen in dev-mode only; production `toJSON()` shares nested objects
returnedData.note: Checked by running without dev-mode: editing `toJSON().nested` changed the cached document (and the memory storage's copy), though the docs call `toJSON()` immutable.

relations.text: schema `ref` with `populate()` or the `field_` getter; one or many
relations.detail: No referential integrity: a removed target populates as `null` (checked by running).

rxState.text: `state` plugin (RxState): schemaless JSON, modifier writes, replicable
rxState.detail: Each write stores the resulting values as an op document under the next sequential id; two replicas writing the same id meet the collection's conflict handler.

pipeline.text: `pipeline` plugin: leader-run handler, checkpointed, blocks the destination

queryLanguage.text: Mango query `{ selector, sort, skip, limit, index }`, matched by mingo
queryLanguage.detail: mingo 7.2.4 is a runtime dependency; RxDB registers 18 of its operators and has no runtime hook to add more (https://rxdb.info/mango-query.html#adding-query-operators).

queryBuilder.detail: 17.6.0 still exposes `all()` (nosql-query-builder.ts:473-475), which emits `$all` and always fails with `unknown query operator $all` (verified); master removes it (orga/changelog/remove-query-builder-all.json).

opSet.detail: `$all` throws `unknown query operator $all`, with or without dev-mode (verified).

opRegex.text: string with `$options`; a `RegExp` instance is refused in dev-mode (QU16)
opRegex.note: Without dev-mode, a `RegExp` instance is normalized to `{}` and the query matches every document (verified on 17.6.0).

opLogical.detail: A top-level `$not` throws `unknown top level operator: $not` (verified).

jsPredicate.text: no `$where` or `$expr`; filter the results in app code
jsPredicate.detail: `$where` and `$expr` throw `unknown query operator` (verified). Filtering after `exec()` runs after `limit`, so a page can come back short.

dottedPaths.text: dot notation in selectors, `sort` (`tags.0`) and indexes
dottedPaths.detail: The docs say a bracket sort path (`tags[0]`) throws QU20 in dev-mode; in 17.6.0 QU20 does not exist: a top-level one throws QU13 in dev-mode, a nested one (`a.b[0]`) and any one outside dev-mode is ignored and rows come back in primary-key order (verified). QU20 is master-only (orga/changelog/dev-mode-throw-on-bracket-sort-path.json).

queryValidation.text: unknown operators throw; field names, `RegExp`, `undefined` and extra keys only in dev-mode
queryValidation.detail: Dev-mode codes QU11 (unknown key), QU13 (field not in schema, top level only), QU16 (RegExp), QU19 (undefined). Without dev-mode a misspelled field returns [] and a RegExp matches everything (verified).

typedQueries.text: `MangoQuery<RxDocType>` checks paths and values; results are typed `RxDocument`s

sort.text: `sort: [{ f: 'asc' | 'desc' }]`: several keys, nested; primary key appended
sort.detail: Without `sort`, RxDB sorts by the best-matching index, then the primary key (rx-query-helper.ts:101-170). A non-indexed sort field works on the free memory storage (verified) and on Dexie, which sorts in memory (dexie-query.ts:181-184).

sortIndex.text: an ascending sort that matches the index walks it and stops at `skip + limit`
sortIndex.note: Any `desc` sort key forces a re-sort of every match, since most storages have no descending index (query-planner.ts:44-48).

topK.detail: Unreleased on master: a bounded heap (`createTopKDocumentsCollector()`) for memory, localstorage, dexie, denokv, foundationdb and sqlite (orga/changelog/top-k-query-sort.json).

streaming.text: `exec()` returns the whole page; keyset paging by hand (`$gt` on the sort key)

count.text: a selector no index satisfies throws `QU14` on Dexie (every storage in dev-mode) unless `allowSlowCount: true`
count.detail: Enforced by dev-mode (QU14) and by storages that report a slow count (Dexie, rx-storage-instance-dexie.ts:251-266); the memory storage counts anyway without dev-mode (verified). `skip`/`limit` are QU15 in dev-mode, ignored otherwise.

projection.text: always whole documents, by design; a `fields` key is QU11 in dev-mode

resultObjects.text: `RxDocument` instances, one per revision, shared across queries
resultObjects.detail: `storageInstance.query(query.getPreparedQuery())` returns plain data with `_rev`/`_meta`, not reactive, not cached.

aggregation.detail: RxPipeline can maintain aggregates in another collection (https://rxdb.info/rx-pipeline.html); TanStack DB's `@tanstack/rxdb-db-collection` adds in-memory `groupBy` (https://rxdb.info/articles/tanstack-db/what-is-tanstack-db.html).

joins.text: one collection per query; `populate()` follows one ref
joins.detail: The IndexedDB article lists 'Joins across stores ✅ populate()' (https://rxdb.info/articles/indexeddb/indexeddb-query.html); populate resolves references, it is not a join. TanStack DB on top of RxDB adds in-memory joins.

encryptedFields.text: encrypted fields cannot be queried; an `$eq` on one silently matches nothing
encryptedFields.detail: Verified with `encryption-crypto-js`: `$eq` and `$regex` 0 rows, `$exists` still 1. The docs suggest a memory-mapped (Premium) unencrypted copy.

indexKind.text: sorted keys: `$eq`, `$gt`…`$lte` and `$in` (min to max) bound the scan

compoundIndexes.text: any index is a field list; `_deleted` and the primary key are added

arrayIndexes.text: refused in dev-mode (`SC36`); an RxPipeline into a mapping collection instead
arrayIndexes.note: Without dev-mode the memory storage fails at `addCollections()` with an uncoded `TypeError`, and Dexie accepts the index on a required field but queries through it find nothing (checked by running).

indexValues.text: strings with `maxLength`, numbers with `minimum`/`maximum`/`multipleOf`, required booleans

indexStorage.text: in the storage: IndexedDB indexes on Dexie (disk), sorted arrays on memory

indexChange.text: a schema change: bump `version` and migrate, or `addCollections()` throws DB6
indexChange.detail: Verified: adding `indexes: ['n']` at the same version is DB6.

planner.text: rates one key range per index, takes the best; `index` forces one

indexCombination.text: one index per query; an `$or` scans a whole index
indexCombination.detail: Verified: the plan for `$or: [{ a }, { b }]` over indexes `a` and `b` has open start and end keys. The docs advise adding a restrictive top-level operator (https://rxdb.info/nosql-performance-tips.html).

coveredQueries.text: `count()` on an index-satisfied selector only; `find()` always reads documents

queryOptimizer.text: Premium (Pro Plus): `findBestIndex()`, run at build time on test data

queryCache.text: `QueryCache`: equal queries share one `RxQuery`; about 100 unobserved ones kept
queryCache.detail: Verified: two `find()` calls with the same selector return the same instance. A custom `cacheReplacementPolicy` per collection.

unique.detail: A `unique: true` keyword on another field is ignored (memory storage inserted the duplicate, verified) and ajv strict mode rejects it as an unknown keyword.

fulltext.detail: Closed source, not verified. The docs say the index is persisted in the collection, built through RxPipeline by the leader tab, and encrypted under an encrypted storage. Third-party alternative: rxdb-flexsearch (docs-src/docs/third-party-plugins.md).

fulltextInQuery.text: `flexSearch.find()` is a separate call; no `$text` operator
fulltextInQuery.detail: `$text` in a selector throws `unknown top level operator: $text` (verified).

vector.text: `rxdb/plugins/vector`: four distance functions; nearest-neighbour search is app code
vector.detail: The article builds the search by hand: embeddings via transformers.js in an RxPipeline, then a full scan or a 'distance to samples' index over regular string indexes.

liveQueries.text: `query.$`: the current result on subscribe, then each new result

liveIncremental.text: EventReduce derives the new result from the change events
liveIncremental.detail: Verified on memory: an unlimited query absorbed four writes with 0 re-runs; a `limit: 3` query re-ran once, when a row had to enter the window. `eventReduce: false` turns it off.

liveDistinct.text: an unchanged result is not emitted

liveCount.text: `count().$`, adjusted from each change event without a re-count
liveCount.detail: Verified: 0 storage re-counts over four writes, with event-reduce on or off.

reactivityPrimitive.text: RxJS observables (`$`); a `reactivity` factory turns them into signals or refs (`$$`)
reactivityPrimitive.detail: Factories ship as reactivity-angular, reactivity-vue, reactivity-preact-signals; the framework list is the platform area's.

liveRemote.text: replicated writes go through the collection's event stream, so `$` updates
liveRemote.detail: Other tabs' writes too, through BroadcastChannel with `multiInstance` (platform area).

replModel.text: document state: pull by checkpoint, push with `assumedMasterState` (fork and master)

wire.text: whole documents with `_deleted`; a push row carries two whole states
wire.detail: `_meta` and `_rev` are stripped; with attachments, full attachment data rides along (src/replication-protocol/index.ts:200-258). Every plugin ships states; none ships operations. The WebRTC page FAQ says it streams "CRDT operations", which the code does not.

replHistory.text: latest state per document; intermediate writes collapse before a push
replHistory.detail: The `crdt` plugin keeps its operations inside the document, so they travel as part of its state.

protocolVersion.text: none in the protocol; checkpoint and payload are the backend's
protocolVersion.detail: RxServer pins the schema version in the endpoint path instead (see Schema check at connect).

schemaHandshake.text: RxServer only: schema version in the URL; older clients get 426 (`outdatedClient$`)
schemaHandshake.note: RxServer compares the integer version only, with no schema hash. Elsewhere every replica must run the same migration, and the backend must accept checkpoints of older versions.
schemaHandshake.detail: https://rxdb.info/migration-schema.html (Migration and Replication): the pull checkpoint is not migrated.

foreignBackend.text: any backend: pull, push and stream handlers over your own database

customTransport.detail: The backend implements the checkpoint query and the `assumedMasterState` compare. The docs' HTTP recipe does not run as written: the server reads `batchSize` where the client sends `limit`, registers push as GET, and emits on an undeclared stream (https://rxdb.info/replication-http.html).

roundTrips.text: pulls until a short page; one push per 100 documents; a re-push per conflict
roundTrips.detail: Every reconnect re-runs the checkpoint iteration (`RESYNC`): at least one pull request.

collectionsPerLink.text: one replication per collection, each with its own requests and stream
collectionsPerLink.detail: GraphQL shares one graphql-ws socket per URL across replications (src/plugins/replication-graphql/graphql-websocket.ts:21-50); `replicateWithWebsocketServer` opens a socket per call; RxServer mounts one endpoint per collection.

replMeta.text: per replication: two checkpoints and the last master state of every document
replMeta.detail: A pull-only replication skips the per-document copies (`skipStoringPullMeta`, src/plugins/replication/index.ts:264).

topology.text: a star of fork–master pairs; WebRTC peers pair up in a mesh

multiMaster.text: WebRTC only; each pair has a hash-chosen master and a fork
multiMaster.note: The WebRTC page says there is "no master-slave concept"; the code makes one peer of every pair the master, and only the other side runs a replication.
multiMaster.detail: The Google Drive and OneDrive plugins need no server of yours either, but the user's drive is then the master.

relay.text: through the local store: a second replication pushes what the first pulled
relay.detail: Only states move; echoes stop when a document equals its assumed master state. With several replications on one collection the docs advise a `push.modifier` so that one replication owns each document.

browserHosts.text: only as the master of a WebRTC pair; other servers are Node

scaleOut.text: processes share one storage; branch servers replicate to a root
scaleOut.note: On the MongoDB and FoundationDB storages a process sees only its own writes (the change-stream relay is a commented-out TODO), so a live stream misses writes made through another process until its next `RESYNC`.
scaleOut.detail: Code reading: rxdb@17.6.0 src/plugins/storage-mongodb/rx-storage-instance-mongodb.ts:124-156; storage-foundationdb/rx-storage-instance-foundationdb.ts:209, 266-268. The scaling page's sample calls `startRxServer()`, which does not exist (`createRxServer` with an `adapter`).

webrtc.detail: Before 17.6.0 the tests were disabled as flaky. Messages are JSON, split above 16 KiB of text with no reassembly cap (connection-handler-simple-peer.ts:164, 570-597). Node needs node-datachannel through `createSimplePeerWrtc()`; browsers need a `process.nextTick` polyfill (:636-643).

signaling.text: self-hosted `ws` server, a public demo server (default), or Nostr relays
signaling.note: Without `signalingServerUrl` the handler uses `wss://signaling.rxdb.info/`, which the code warns is for demos only; the official quickstart app uses it.
signaling.detail: Nostr signaling arrived in 17.6.0 (relays required, no defaults). The p2pcf and WebTorrent handlers are commented out.

p2pRoom.text: full mesh: one replication per pair, N(N−1)/2 in all, no cap
