p2pRoom.detail: Each pair keeps its own checkpoint (`collection||topic||peerToken`); the master side of a pair has no replication state to observe (webrtc-types.ts:97-105).

ice.text: simple-peer's Google and Twilio STUN by default; no TURN

websocket.text: `replication-websocket`: RxDB to RxDB, a Node server, no authentication
websocket.note: The server ignores the client's `auth` message, and one message naming an unknown collection crashes the Node process (both checked by running).
websocket.detail: The docs position it for server-to-server use. Every tab opens the socket before leader election (websocket-client.ts:100, 161-183).

http.text: your endpoints under `replicateRxCollection`; RxServer serves pull, push and SSE

graphql.text: `replication-graphql`; live through graphql-ws; schema and query generators
graphql.note: With `pull.batchSize` unset the query asks for 20 documents while the core stops at a page under 100, so a cycle pulls only 20 (checked by running).

couchdb.detail: Not the CouchDB replication protocol: only winning revisions cross, no attachments, one database per collection. The url must end with `/`, which the docs' examples lack (index.ts:85-97).

firestore.note: The push compare runs inside `runTransaction` without using the transaction, so a write landing between its read and commit is overwritten (code reading).

supabase.text: `replication-supabase`: PostgREST compare-and-set; Realtime for live rows
supabase.detail: The Realtime channel is not filtered by `pull.queryBuilder`, hard DELETEs never reach clients, and object or array fields cannot be updated by push (code reading).

appwrite.text: `replication-appwrite`: browser only; updates read then write, not atomic
appwrite.detail: The non-atomic update is a TODO in the code (index.ts:188-193). `appwrite` is imported at runtime but declared nowhere in rxdb's package.json.

mongodb.text: `replication-mongodb` (Node): change streams; push in a transaction; replica set
mongodb.detail: Deletes are real `deleteOne`s, read back from the change stream's pre-image. A replicator offline past the oplog window cannot resume its token.

nats.text: `replication-nats`: a subject per document; updates checked by sequence
nats.detail: Inserts publish with no sequence expectation, so two concurrent first writes of one id are not detected; the stream keeps every version unless limited (code reading).

gdrive.text: `replication-google-drive`, beta: JSON files and a lock file in the user's Drive
gdrive.detail: Live pulls come only from WebRTC pings between devices already connected; the lock file is not released on error (60 s timeout in code, 10 s in the docs). Beta is stated on the page only.

onedrive.text: `replication-microsoft-onedrive`, beta: the same file-and-lock scheme over Graph
onedrive.detail: Unlike Google Drive, document updates carry no `If-Match`, so an overlap after a stale lock is not caught (document-handling.ts:143-152).

conflictDetect.text: the master compares `assumedMasterState` with its own (`isEqual`, deep-equal)

conflictResolve.text: `conflictHandler.resolve` on the client; the default keeps the master's document
conflictResolve.note: Some RxDB pages call the default last-write-wins; the code keeps the server's state whatever its time (https://rxdb.info/articles/zero-latency-local-first.html).

customMerge.text: any function per collection; the `crdt` plugin brings its own

conflictWhere.text: on the client (fork); the server only detects
conflictWhere.detail: Over WebRTC the side that lost the hash comparison resolves, so every peer needs the same deterministic handler.

conflictEvents.text: `conflict$`: each conflict the server reported, with the handler's output

serverCompare.text: per plugin: atomic on RxDB storages, CouchDB, Supabase, MongoDB; not Firestore, Appwrite
serverCompare.detail: NATS checks updates by subject sequence but not inserts; Google Drive and OneDrive serialise through a lock file; GraphQL and custom HTTP leave it to your resolver. A push batch is not atomic: a non-409 error after valid rows were written throws (index.ts:307-324).

causality.text: none across replicas: a compare-and-set against the master's last state
causality.detail: `_rev` (a height plus the instance token) is local and stripped before a push; the docs liken revisions to Lamport clocks.

clocks.text: unused by the protocol; backend checkpoints and LWW handlers bring their own
clocks.detail: The docs say client clocks can never be trusted and ask the backend to overwrite `updatedAt`; the quickstart's LWW handler compares `Date.now()` stamps from clients.

live.text: `pull.stream$`, yours or a plugin's; `RESYNC` when events may be missed
live.detail: Without `stream$` a live replication pulls only at start and on `reSync()`. Firestore, MongoDB and the Drive plugins emit only `RESYNC`, never documents.

resume.text: a checkpoint pull (`RESYNC`) after each reconnect; the stream is not resumed

restart.text: checkpoints stored per `replicationIdentifier`; a new state with the same id continues

reconnect.text: each plugin's own; a custom `stream$` must reconnect and emit `RESYNC`

retry.text: each pull or push error goes to `error$`, retried after `retryTime` (5 s), forever
retry.detail: A fixed delay, cut short by the browser `online` event; no exponential backoff in the core.

dup.text: states, not ops: pages ordered by checkpoint, repeats harmless
dup.detail: A push re-sent after it already landed must be tolerated by the backend; with RxDB's own handlers it returns as a conflict that resolves to the same state.

offline.text: local writes; on reconnect the latest state of each changed document is pushed

bootstrap.text: a checkpoint iteration from scratch over the backend's current documents

longOffline.text: the same checkpoint pull; the backend must keep soft-deleted documents

batch.detail: WebRTC defaults to 20; GraphQL asks for 20 while the core expects 100 (see GraphQL).

flow.text: no explicit caps; four push batches in flight; queued changes coalesce per document

partial.text: one replication per scope, filtered by your backend; RxServer `queryModifier`
partial.detail: Firestore takes `pull.filter`; Supabase `pull.queryBuilder` (its live stream is not filtered); the other plugins replicate whole collections.

partialLive.text: one stream per replication, scoped by your backend
partialLive.source: https://rxdb.info/partial-sync.html (Real Time Updates with a Pull Stream)

revoke.text: no signal: the client keeps its copy; RxServer then refuses its pushes
revoke.detail: On that 403 the client emits `forbidden$` and cancels the whole replication (src/plugins/replication-server/helpers.ts:21-26).

oneWay.text: omit `push` or `pull`; pull-only stores no per-document meta

deletes.text: `_deleted: true` with the whole document; the backend must keep it
deletes.source: https://rxdb.info/replication.html (Data layout on the server); rxdb@17.6.0 src/plugins/replication/replication-helper.ts:33-63
deletes.detail: `deletedField` renames the flag (Firestore and NATS hard-code `_deleted` despite their docs); MongoDB maps real deletes through pre-images; Supabase drops hard DELETEs. The `cleanup` plugin purges local tombstones after 31 days.

replAttachments.text: in the protocol; only Google Drive and OneDrive carry them intact
replAttachments.note: Over the WebSocket and WebRTC plugins attachment data is silently corrupted, since Blobs pass through `JSON.stringify` (checked by running); RxServer, GraphQL, Appwrite and MongoDB drop it.

lifecycle.detail: In 17.6.0 `start()` after `cancel()` silently does nothing; the live docs describe master's `RC_START_CANCELED` (orga/changelog/replication-start-after-cancel-throws.json).

awaitSync.detail: In a tab that is not the leader `awaitInSync()` does not resolve while another tab replicates (https://rxdb.info/replication.html).

resync.text: `reSync()` runs a checkpoint pull; `emitEvent()` feeds the stream by hand

replMultiTab.text: only the elected leader tab replicates (`waitForLeadership: true`); others see its writes
replMultiTab.note: A visible tab that is not the leader also starts replicating (`toggleOnDocumentVisible`, on by default), so two tabs can replicate at once (code reading).
replMultiTab.detail: src/plugins/replication/index.ts:828-857. broadcast-channel prefers Web Locks; on Node 24 these did not exclude a second process in a local test, so separate Node processes may each lead.

serverProduct.text: RxServer: the separate `rxdb-server` package (SSPL), over an RxDatabase
serverProduct.detail: Free of charge, but SSPL section 13 obliges anyone offering it as a service to publish their service's source.

serverRuntime.text: Node, through the Express adapter; Deno, Bun and Electron claimed, untested

adapters.text: Express free (SSPL); Fastify and Koa are Premium (Pro Plus)

remoteQuery.text: RxServer REST endpoint and `client-rest`; live results over SSE

serverStorage.text: any RxStorage of the server's RxDatabase: memory, MongoDB, FoundationDB…

atRest.text: per field (schema `encrypted: [...]`): free `encryption-crypto-js`; WebCrypto is Premium (Pro)
atRest.detail: Both are wrappers around an RxStorage (`wrappedKeyEncryptionCryptoJsStorage`, `wrappedKeyEncryptionWebCryptoStorage`); a schema with `encrypted` fields and no password throws `EN3`.

encScope.text: the listed fields only; primary key, other fields, `_meta`, `_rev` stay plain
encScope.detail: Checked by running: `{"id":"u1","name":"alice","ssn":"U2FsdGVkX1…"}` on disk. A nested path encrypts the whole object at it as one string. The replication meta copy (`docData`) is encrypted whole when the collection encrypts (src/replication-protocol/meta-instance.ts:94-95).

cipher.text: free: AES-256-CBC, MD5 key derivation, no MAC; AES-GCM selectable in Premium
cipher.note: crypto-js's passphrase mode derives key and IV with EVP_BytesToKey (MD5, one iteration) and authenticates nothing, and crypto-js is discontinued; the page calls the plugin 'tamper proof'.
cipher.detail: Checked by running: every encrypted value starts with OpenSSL's `Salted__` header. The Premium WebCrypto plugin takes `{ algorithm: 'AES-CTR' | 'AES-CBC' | 'AES-GCM', password }`; its key derivation is closed source.

keyOffDisk.text: `password` given at `createRxDatabase`, kept in memory; an unsalted SHA-256 of it is stored
keyOffDisk.note: The stored hash lets anyone with the files test password guesses offline at SHA-256 speed (checked: it equals `sha256(JSON.stringify(password))`).
keyOffDisk.detail: Minimum length 8 (`EN2`). A wrong password fails with `DB1` at `addCollections()`, not at `createRxDatabase()` (checked). The password property is non-enumerable.

keyRotation.text: not possible; migrate into a new database, or wrap a meta-password

encExport.text: the `backup` plugin and `exportJSON()` write encrypted fields decrypted
encExport.detail: Both read through the collection, above the encryption wrapper; the docs say a dump holds encrypted fields in plain text.

encSync.text: encrypted fields replicate decrypted; the backend receives plaintext
encSync.detail: Checked by running: a push handler received `{"ssn":"123-45-6789","card":{"num":"4111"}}` from a collection that stores both encrypted.

e2ee.text: none; replication reads the decrypted documents
e2ee.detail: `push.modifier` and `pull.modifier` (src/plugins/replication/index.ts:219-220,324-352) could encrypt on the wire, and https://rxdb.info/articles/case-studies/venice-ai.html sketches such a design with a backend that compares a plaintext hash; nothing ships, and push conflicts do not pass through `pull.modifier` (index.ts:423).

signing.text: none; Nostr keys sign WebRTC signaling, not documents

nodeIdentity.text: random tokens (`storageToken`, instance token); a key only through the Nostr handler
nodeIdentity.detail: The instance token is the suffix of every `_rev` and the `creator` of `crdt` ops.

tamper.text: none; `_rev` is a height plus the writer's instance token

authn.text: RxServer `authHandler(headers)`, re-run before each streamed event
authn.note: Defaults are open: with no `authHandler` every request is admitted, and the Express adapter's default CORS reflects any request origin with credentials. The documented `validUntil` is never read. The server listens on localhost unless told otherwise. The `replication-websocket` server has no auth at all.
authn.source: rxdb-server@17.6.0 src/plugins/server/index.ts:17-22, helper.ts:36-55, endpoint-replication.ts:218-238, rx-server.ts:29, adapter-express/index.ts:18-33; rxdb@17.6.0 src/plugins/replication-websocket/websocket-server.ts:102-104; https://rxdb.info/rx-server.html#auth-handler; https://rxdb.info/replication-websocket.html
authn.detail: `validUntil` appears only in types.ts:61 and the default handler. RxServer is a separate package, `rxdb-server`, under SSPL.

peerValidation.text: `isPeerValid(peer)`; the Nostr handler verifies each peer's public key
peerValidation.note: Once valid, a peer reads and writes every document of the collection.
peerValidation.detail: The result is cached per peer; a throwing `isPeerValid` counts as false. With the simple-peer signaling server peers are not identified.

access.detail: Only RxServer; with the other replication plugins your backend filters. The matcher also guards the stored state a push targets, so a conflict answer cannot leak a foreign document (endpoint-replication.ts:155-170).

writeRules.text: RxServer `changeValidator(authData, change)`: one refused row is 403 for the push
writeRules.detail: Writes must also match `queryModifier`, before and after. The validator must be synchronous; the docs' readonly-field example throws instead of returning false.

serverValidation.text: only if the server's storage is wrapped in a `validate-*` plugin
serverValidation.note: Collection hooks do not run on replicated writes, and a 422 throws after the valid rows of the batch were written.

serverAuth.text: RxServer is the master: a refused push reaches no client
serverAuth.note: Over WebRTC there is no master: each peer's storage decides alone.

limits.text: none in RxServer; `$regex` queries refused against ReDoS
limits.detail: A pull's `limit` comes from the query string uncapped; express.json()'s default 100 kB body is the only bound on a push.

purge.note: A removed document keeps all its data in the tombstone until then, and forever without the plugin; `cleanup(0)` forces it once replications are in sync.
purge.detail: With the `crdt` plugin the tombstone also carries every past value in its op list (checked by running).

purgeReplicas.text: cleanup is local; a delete replicates as a tombstone with the full data
purgeReplicas.detail: Checked by running: the push handler received `{"id":"a","email":"bob@example.com","_deleted":true}` for a removed document.

history.text: latest revision only; the `crdt` plugin keeps every op in the document
history.note: Op compaction is not implemented, so a `crdt` document carries every past value, in its tombstone too.

audit.text: none; `crdt` ops carry the writer's storage token and a time

proto.detail: Checked by running: `insert`, `update({ $set: { '__proto__.x': 1 } })` (refused), `incrementalPatch` and a selector left `Object.prototype` clean.

malformed.text: only with a `validate-*` wrapper: the invalid document is dropped (`RC_PULL`)
malformed.note: Without a wrapper a pulled document with wrong types and extra fields is stored as sent (checked by running).
malformed.detail: With ajv the valid documents of the batch landed, the invalid one raised `RC_PULL` (422) on `error$` and was not pulled again.

skew.text: no peer clocks: conflicts compare document states

hooks.text: pre/post `insert`/`save`/`remove`, plus `postCreate`; many, series or parallel
hooks.detail: Checked by running: a hook mutates the plain data and throws to abort; `incrementalPatch`, `update` and query `update` run `preSave`; `upsert` of an existing document runs `preInsert` then `preSave`. The page's claim that validation runs per changed field is outdated: the `validate-*` wrappers check whole documents.

replHooks.text: `pull.modifier` per replication; collection hooks skip pulled documents
replHooks.detail: Checked by running: pulled documents ran no `preInsert`/`preSave`. The modifier transforms but cannot drop a document; the global plugin hooks `preStorageWrite` (synchronous) and `preReplicationMasterWrite` see replicated rows too.

outHook.text: `push.modifier` transforms a document or drops it (`null`)

readHooks.text: none; `postCreate` runs when a document object is built

plugins.note: Plugins are process-wide and cannot be removed.

errors.text: `RxError.code`: 215 codes; the message text only with `dev-mode`
errors.detail: Counted from `ERROR_MESSAGES` in the installed 17.6.0; https://rxdb.info/errors.html (master) lists 218.

logging.text: Premium `logger` storage wrapper (Pro Plus); the core logs nothing

otel.source: rxdb@17.6.0 src; rxdb-server@17.6.0 src (no tracer or meter)

stats.text: no stats API; replication states have `active$` and `awaitInSync()`

diagPII.text: error messages embed their parameters: documents, pushed rows, password hashes
diagPII.note: Checked by running: a wrong password's `DB1` carries both the given and the stored password hash.

vue.detail: Moved from Premium into the core in 17.0.0.

angular.source: rxdb@17.6.0 package.json:393; src/plugins/reactivity-angular/index.ts; https://rxdb.info/articles/angular-database.html; examples/angular (CI, with SSR)

svelte.text: no plugin; a Svelte 5 example app runs in CI

signals.text: `reactivity` option: Preact signals plugin, or your own factory; no Solid adapter
signals.detail: Moved from Premium into the core in 17.0.0. `rxdb-solid` on the third-party page is about Solid pods, not SolidJS (https://rxdb.info/third-party-plugins.html).

tanstack.detail: Third-party to RxDB: MIT, in the TanStack/db repository. The page says it needs rxdb ≥16.17.2; npm's 0.1.111 declares the peer `rxdb >=17.0.0`. rxdb.info has 19 TanStack DB articles (articles/tanstack-db/*).

devMode.text: `rxdb/plugins/dev-mode`: readable errors, deep-freeze, schema and query checks
devMode.note: Without it an error carries only its code. With it, the storage must be wrapped in a schema validator (`DVM1`), and in browsers it adds a tracking iframe (see Calls to the vendor).
devMode.detail: DVM1: src/plugins/dev-mode/error-messages.ts:1140-1145, thrown at src/plugins/dev-mode/index.ts:133. ERROR-MESSAGES.md in the npm package lists every code.

testing.text: memory storage; `rxdb/plugins/test-utils` (fixtures, replication test suite); `using` closes databases
testing.note: The testing page's multi-tab simulation needs `ignoreDuplicate: true`, which throws `DB9` unless dev-mode is on, and the 13-collection limit counts every database a test run leaves open.

ci.text: 74 test files per storage; Linux, Windows, browsers, Bun, Deno, 11 example apps; no coverage gate

docs.text: 271 pages, about 463,000 words: 98 articles, 46 landing pages
docs.source: https://rxdb.info sitemap (mirrored 2026-10); rxdb@17.6.0 docs-src/docs (200 markdown files)

examples.text: 13 example apps; 11 run in CI: Angular, React, React Native, Electron, Tauri, Vue, Svelte…
examples.detail: CI-run: angular, electron, graphql, ionic, node, react, react-native (Expo), svelte, tauri, vite-vanilla-ts, vue. Not run: flutter (job commented out), supabase.

breakingMajors.note: Majors 13, 14, 16 and 17 each told users of some or all storages to move their stored data with the `migration-storage` plugin or to re-sync it from the backend.
breakingMajors.detail: 8.0 2018-09-18, 9.0 2020-05-16, 10.0 2021-07-20, 11.0 2022-01-03, 12.0 2022-04-26, 13.0 2022-09-16, 14.0 2023-02-08, 15.0 2023-12-20, 16.0 2025-01-02, 17.0 2026-03-30; before that six majors (2.0 to 7.0) in 2017. 13.0: stored data of earlier versions is not compatible. 14.0: schema hashing changed, every schema needs a version bump and a migration strategy. 16.0: SQLite, Filesystem-Node and OPFS data must be migrated. 17.0: OPFS, Filesystem-Node and IndexedDB-with-attachments data must be migrated. 9.0.0 says majors bundle the breaking changes so users upgrade in one block.

releaseCadence.text: about monthly: 17.0 to 17.6 between March and October 2026
releaseCadence.detail: Release headings in CHANGELOG.md per year: 107 in 2022, 61 in 2023, 71 in 2024, 26 in 2025, 7 in 2026 up to 17.6.0. Plugins ship as beta and leave it at a major: 17.0 took the CRDT plugin, RxPipeline, attachment replication, the Supabase, Appwrite and MongoDB replications and the MongoDB, DenoKV and Filesystem-Node storages out of beta (https://rxdb.info/releases/17.0.0.html).

freeTierHistory.text: Premium since 12.0 (2022); Worker storage moved in at 14.0; collection cap since 16.0
freeTierHistory.source: https://rxdb.info/releases/12.0.0.html; https://rxdb.info/releases/14.0.0.html; https://rxdb.info/releases/15.0.0.html; https://rxdb.info/releases/16.0.0.html; https://rxdb.info/releases/17.0.0.html; rxdb@17.6.0 src/plugins/utils/utils-premium.ts:6
freeTierHistory.note: The open-source cap on open collections was 16 in 16.0 and is 13 since 17.0. Two features went the other way: `migration-storage` (15.0) and the Vue and Preact signals plugins (17.0) became free.
freeTierHistory.detail: Worker storage shipped free as `rxdb/plugins/worker` in 11.0 (https://rxdb.info/releases/11.0.0.html). Later Premium additions: query optimizer (12.4.1), memory-synced storage (12.6.11, removed in 16.0), localstorage meta optimizer (13.4.4), OPFS storage (14.7.0), logger (15.0), fulltext search (15.32.0) (CHANGELOG.md:1437,1373,1219,883,515). Since 15.21.0 the free Dexie storage logs a console warning that points to Premium (CHANGELOG.md:608; src/plugins/storage-dexie/rx-storage-instance-dexie.ts:84-93). The free SQLite trial went from 300 to 500 documents in 17.4.0 (CHANGELOG.md:136) and also stops after 500 operations per instance (src/plugins/storage-sqlite/sqlite-storage-instance.ts:57-58,113-117).

productionUsers.text: 10 testimonials (Readwise, Nutrien, Venice.ai, …); one case study
productionUsers.detail: The Venice.ai case study names no license, data sizes or write rates; its "IndexedDB" and "SQLite" links go to the Premium storage pages, and its end-to-end encrypted sync is planned, not built.

commercialSupport.text: paid: €180 one-hour consulting; Enterprise SLA, 24-hour first response
commercialSupport.detail: Enterprise also lists a named engineer, architecture review, priority fixes and source-code access; the consulting page matches clients with partner agencies for contract work. No free trial; licenses are annual (premium.html). The couchbase-alternative page calls Premium a one-time purchase, which premium.html contradicts.
commercialSupport.note: The Pro and Pro Plus agreement says 'No Technical Support'; free users get GitHub and Discord, and a bug report is expected as a pull request with a failing test.

communityHelp.text: Discord, GitHub; a bug report needs a PR with a failing test
communityHelp.detail: The chat rules forbid direct messages to the maintainer for support; the site shows about 1,300 Discord members.

thirdPartyPlugins.detail: The list still names `loki-async-reference-adapter`, for the LokiJS storage that 16.0 removed.

community.text: 23,412 GitHub stars; 63,815 npm downloads in the week to 2026-10-18

importFromOtherDbs.text: migration guides only; `importJSON()` takes an RxDB dump of the same schema
importFromOtherDbs.note: No converter ships: the Realm, PouchDB, Dexie, LokiJS, NeDB, GUN and other guides read the old store and call `bulkInsert`/`bulkUpsert` by hand.
importFromOtherDbs.detail: `importJSON()` throws JD2 when the dump's schema hash differs. `migration-storage` moves data between RxDB storages and RxDB majors, not from other databases. The SEM pages garealm1-3 target teams leaving Realm (CHANGELOG.md:150-152).

benchmarks.text: its own storages only; no machine, browser or date given
benchmarks.note: Most measured storages are Premium (OPFS, IndexedDB, SQLite, Filesystem); the free localStorage storage that most guides use is not measured.
benchmarks.detail: The harness is open source (3000 docs, 40 runs; test/performance.test.ts). Articles also cite 2024 raw-API numbers from Chrome 128 as RxDB-vs-SQLite-WASM evidence (https://rxdb.info/articles/rxdb-vs-sqlite-wasm-vs-pglite.html), and the vector-search numbers come from a demo repository pinned to rxdb 15.32.0 (https://rxdb.info/articles/javascript-vector-database.html).

webmcp.text: `rxdb/plugins/webmcp`: query, count, changes, insert, upsert, delete tools per collection; `readOnly`
webmcp.note: WebMCP is an experimental browser API; where `navigator.modelContext` is missing the docs point to the `@mcp-b/global` polyfill.

agentDocs.text: `llms.txt` plus three topic files; `ERROR-MESSAGES.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md` in the package
agentDocs.source: rxdb@17.6.0 docs-src/docusaurus.config.ts:152-178; scripts/generate-error-messages.mjs:15,32; npm rxdb@17.6.0 ERROR-MESSAGES.md; https://rxdb.info/releases/17.0.0.html
agentDocs.note: In the 17.6.0 tarball all 215 entries of ERROR-MESSAGES.md are headed `## undefined`, and COL23 states a limit of 16 collections where the code enforces 13.
agentDocs.detail: The 17.0.0 notes say errors carry `cause`, `fix` and `docs` properties. In the code `RxError` has `code`, `message`, `url` and `parameters`; dev-mode appends cause, fix and docs to the message text (src/rx-error.ts:51-69; src/plugins/dev-mode/index.ts:100-122).
